hook.line: Money and work always end up on the table, and someone has to say who gets what. Spanish keeps two ideas apart: cutting something into parts, and sharing it out among people.
hook.en: Shall we split the bill in half?

examples.es: Partimos la cuenta por la mitad.
examples.en: We split the bill in half.

examples.es: Repartieron la herencia entre los hijos.
examples.en: They shared out the inheritance among the children.

examples.es: Dividimos el grupo en tres equipos.
examples.en: We divided the group into three teams.

examples.es: Vale repartió los pasteles entre los clientes.
examples.en: Vale shared out the pastries among the customers.

examples.es: Tomás partió el pan por la mitad.
examples.en: Tomás split the bread in half.

rule:
English says "split" for everything. Spanish asks what you are doing.

Cutting into parts: *partir* or *dividir*, then *por la mitad* or *en* plus the number: *Dividimos el grupo en tres equipos*.

Handing out to people: *repartir* plus *entre* and the people: *Repartieron la herencia entre los hijos*.

For paying, *a medias* means half each.
smallPrint: Teachers call *entre* here a preposition of distribution: the recipients sit after it.

readAndPick.es: Partimos la cuenta por la mitad.
options: We paid the whole bill.
We split the bill in half.
We split the bill in three.

readAndPick.es: Dividimos el grupo en tres equipos.
options: We divided the group into three teams.
We divided the group into two teams.
We joined three teams.

readAndPick.es: Repartieron la herencia entre los hijos.
options: They cut the inheritance in half.
They left the inheritance to one child.
They shared out the inheritance among the children.
Shall I pay it all?
Shall we pay later?
Shall we go halves?

readAndPick.es: Vale repartió los pasteles entre los clientes.
options: Vale handed out the pastries among the customers.
Vale cut the pastries in half.
Vale ate the pastries with the customers.

readAndPick.es: Tomás partió el pan por la mitad.
options: Tomás shared the bread out among the customers.
Tomás split the bread in half.
Tomás split the bread in three.

readAndPick.es: Repartimos el trabajo entre los tres.
options: We did the work in three days.
We gave all the work to the third one.
We shared the work out among the three of us.
They split the bill four ways.
They split the bill in half.
They paid the bill for four.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right word and type the whole sentence: *Partimos la cuenta ___ la mitad.* (*por* or *entre*)
yourTurn.answer: Partimos la cuenta por la mitad.
yourTurn.why: *Por la mitad* is the set phrase for cutting something in two.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: They shared out the inheritance among the children.
yourTurn.answer: Repartieron la herencia entre los hijos.
yourTurn.why: Handing out to people is *repartir* plus *entre* and the people.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right word and type the whole sentence: *Dividimos el grupo ___ tres equipos.* (*en* or *entre*)
yourTurn.answer: Dividimos el grupo en tres equipos.
yourTurn.why: Cutting into a number of parts takes *en* plus the number.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale shared out the pastries among the customers.
yourTurn.answer: Vale repartió los pasteles entre los clientes.
yourTurn.why: The pastries go to people, so *repartió* and *entre*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Shall we go halves?
yourTurn.why: *A medias* is the everyday way to share a bill fifty-fifty.

yourTurn.prompt: Put it about Tomás: *Partimos el pan por la mitad.* Say: Tomás split the bread in half.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás partió el pan por la mitad.
accept: Partió el pan por la mitad.
yourTurn.why: One person did it in the past, so *partió*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Repartimos el trabajo entre los tres.* Say: We didn't share out the work among the three of us.
yourTurn.answer: No repartimos el trabajo entre los tres.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of the verb.

pitfalls.wrong: Repartieron la herencia en los hijos.
pitfalls.right: Repartieron la herencia entre los hijos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When the people who receive are named, Spanish uses *entre*, not *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: Partimos la cuenta en la mitad.
pitfalls.right: Partimos la cuenta por la mitad.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "in half", but Spanish says *por la mitad*.

pitfalls.wrong: Dividimos el grupo por tres equipos.
pitfalls.right: Dividimos el grupo en tres equipos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The parts you end up with follow *en*.

personal: Think of the last time you split something with someone. Say it with *partimos…* or *repartimos…*
